page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column; marginal notes in the right margin (partly cut off by the binding and the neighbouring page edge). Running head at top. Closing italic lines centred below the text. A catchword-like line at the foot right is not clearly legible.

main_text.p: escam, & illum bibere potum, in Christo manere & illum manentem in se habere. Qui autem per hoc qui non manet in Christo, & in quo non manet Christus, procul dubio nec manducat spiritualiter carnem ejus, nec bibit ejus sanguinem, licet carnaliter visibiliter premat dentibus Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Christi: sed magis tantum Sacramentum ad judicium sibi manducat & bibit, quia immundus praesumpsit ad Christi accedere Sacramenta, quae alios non digne sumit, nisi qui mundus est. Atque hinc dicit, secundum quendam modum Sacramentum corporis Christi corpus Christi esse, Sacramentum sanguinis Christi sanguinem Christi esse Epist. 23. Hac ergo sacramentali phrasi impii dicuntur manducare corpus Christi & bibere sanguinem ejus, non revera. Hanc rem fuse & eleganter prosequutus est ex sententia antiquitatis & Patrum orthodoxus confensus cap. 9. quem videat qui plura desiderat.

page.notes: Marginal notes in the right margin are cut off and only partly legible (fragments such as "A:", "nec", "visib.", "corp.", "Christi", "Epist."); they are not transcribed. The word "Hac" and some marginal words near the binding are doubtful. The final word of the page "CAP" at lower right is a partly visible catchword and is not transcribed with certainty. Scan edges and show-through from the facing page are ignored.
